posts.name: Killswitch
posts.cooked:
My first game with Hunted Naturalist was with Rhino form in hand, and I got Resilient hide and Natural Born Vigor out shortly after. So, two powers + two forms + two plays each turn. It was a good time.

On the flip side, if for whatever reason a form is replaced or destroyed, you've gotta fish it out of the trash with another hero, but even then you're guaranteed a form use, and still have two plays each turn.

posts.name: Trajector
posts.cooked:
That mimics my first game with Hunted Naturalist - I loved it! It was a Vengeance-style game, and he started with the Crocodile in hand. I played it and started using his base power to double-form with the +1 damage modifier. Only a few rounds in, though, I drew the Rhinoceros. Since I had Resilient Hide in play already, I turned into a rhino and got some Rhinodile Indomitable Force action going on to protect Young Legacy from Greazer’s contract. I stayed a Rhino for the rest of that game and used both my double-form options for Crafty Assaults and various croc effects.

Hunted Naturalist was definitely MVP of that game. He was hard to hit and hard-hitting.

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
Remember it is end of next turn, so you can have a form in play, activate another form, then for your next turn power activate the third form and play a one-shot.  Then if you have the second power use throw down Natural Form's Power for all three effects.

With 2 of Croc, Powe and Vigor in play and the other one and Primal Charge in hand and a banked form active from the last turn you can deal 2 targets 2 damage, 1 target 3 damage one target 4 damage, draw 6 cards and regain 2hp.

It is a good time.

I find Bestial Shift less good, and Natural Form's Power much better with this version of Naturalist.

This promo also turned Naturalist from a Hero I viewed as really strong, but not as fun to a really fun hero who goes crazy if he has a form in play.

posts.name: McBehrer
posts.cooked: I use 10-sided dice. One of each color, to represent the symbols, and when I use the power I set it to 2. At the end of his turns, the numbers tick down one. So, 2 becomes 1, and goes to 0. That way I can tell which one I activated this turn and which I activated last turn, and they expire at the right time. If a form is out, I set it to 8 and turn it sideways.

posts.name: Spiff
posts.cooked:
Just to make sure I understand how it goes (in case I want to make a tracker), is this correct:

Turn 1:

  • There are no forms in effect.
  • The player chooses a form (croc) on their Power phase.  Croc is in effect during their turn and until the end of their next turn.

Turn 2:

  • Croc is still in effect from last round.
  • The player chooses a form (rhino) on their Power phase.  During the player's turn, both croc and rhino are in effect.
  • At the end of their turn, croc goes away but rhino stays in effect until the end of their next turn.

This means that Naturalist will only ever have two forms in effect from the Desperate Prey power (not counting anything they'd get from an actual form card in play) while it's their turn, and when it's not their turn they can only ever have one form in effect.

Do I have it surrounded?
